more_info.overview: Steviol glycosides are a group of sweet substances based on a steviol structure; the current food-additive list distinguishes several production-specific preparations. It provides sweetness when added to the food or used in a table-top sweetener preparation. The specified leaf-extract form is produced by extracting stevia leaves with water, purifying the extract and recrystallising the glycosides. Other currently authorised steviol-glycoside forms have their own specifications. The specified material is supplied as white powder. Only a limited amount dissolves in water, according to the specification.
more_info.daily_intake: 0–4 mg steviol equivalents/kg body weight/day, combined steviol glycosides (JECFA, 2026).
more_info.origin: The specified leaf-extract form is produced by extracting stevia leaves with water, purifying the extract and recrystallising the glycosides. Other currently authorised steviol-glycoside forms have their own specifications.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: For the specified stevia-leaf extract, the starting material is plant derived. This does not establish the source or religious certification of every preparation in the wider steviol-glycoside group.
more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
EU permission applies to the specified E960a–E960d preparations under the 2026 consolidated rules.
more_info.side_effects:
In 2026, JECFA retained the intake limit and did not identify new toxicity evidence requiring a revision.
A conservative high-consumption estimate for children exceeded the limit; its significance was qualified by exposure-model uncertainty.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain cocoa and Chocolate products as covered by Directive 2000/36/EC; other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; fruit nectars as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable nectars and similar products; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products.
The permitted food categories and limits differ between the separately specified preparations. These listed examples do not establish the prevalence of the ingredient in retail foods.
